facts.fact: WHO's Chad office reports that during the 2024-2025 biennium its support contributed to the validation of the 2024 statistical yearbook, the updating of the reporting tools and their integration into DHIS2, and the validation of a procedures manual for managing health information; it gives no count of facilities or districts.

WHO's Chad office reports that a national digital health strategy was adopted during the 2024-2025 biennium, with WHO supporting the national strategic plan for digital health, its operational plans and a law on health data protection; the report does not say which systems the plan names.

systems.tiers: not stated; cited as the source of administrative vaccination coverage by province and of antenatal and maternal figures for the 15 supported provinces (2024-2025)

systems.platform: DHIS2 Tracker on Android tablets, online and offline, with a central production server holding all patient files and the imported historical HIV database
systems.tiers: focal points trained at 160 TB treatment sites and 482 HIV sites; 7,475 HIV patients and 21,824 TB patients registered (2024-2025)
54 GeneXpert machines connected nationally, 54 laboratory technicians trained (2024-2025)
eight health districts in eastern Chad including refugee camps; 64 alerts detected, 68.6% handled within 48 hours; mobile phones supplied to 85 staff (2024-2025)

systems.owner: not stated; WHO preparing it with regional and headquarters experts
systems.tiers: pilot hospitals, planned for 2026; what is to be digitised is not described
